 - The IRGC said the carrier ‘suffered a massive fire in the engine room and propulsion system’.
 - Trump says he won’t attack Iran before the US midterm elections
 - Trump has doubled down on remarks that Washington stopped Iran from deploying a nuclear weapon.
 - Without evidence, Trump said Tehran “would have blown up the Middle East” and then “headed for our country” had the US and Israel not launched a military campaign.
 - The president also repeated comments about Tehran striking Los Angeles and San Diego that sparked bipartisan backlash earlier this week.
 - “They would have probably hit places like San Diego, Los Angeles first,” he said.
 - US Democrat Senator Chris Murphy has called the US’s war against Iran a “national humiliation”.
 - In a post on X, Murphy said, “It’s making us less safe and driving up prices on everything.”
 - He claimed US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth denied him access to US military bases and leaders during a visit to the Middle East to “hide the truth”.
 - Murphy said, “This war is not working, we are losing.”
 - He added, “There is a cover up campaign underway right now, so the American people don’t see the actual cost of this war.”
 - He said that there had been substantial damage, running into billions of dollars at US bases in the Gulf and demanded transparency about the destruction caused by the Iran war.
 - “Not a single member of Congress is allowed in [to US bases] to see that damage because Trump doesn’t want Americans to know what a debacle this has been,” Murphy said.
 - The foreign affairs ministry of Yemen’s internationally recognised government has expressed its “full solidarity” with Saudi Arabia, following the Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport that killed three citizens.
 - In a statement, the ministry said it supported the kingdom “to take legitimate measures to protect its security, sovereignty, citizens and residents within it” and emphasised that targeting airports “reveals the approach of a terrorist group that does not hesitate to terrorise the innocent and damage vital facilities”.
 - “Expanding the scope of these attacks will not deter Yemenis from restoring their state, nor will it provide an escape for its coup project from its crisis,” the statement added.
 - US President Donald Trump says he’ll soon release news about diesel and claimed that nearly record-high prices will soon come “tumbling” down.
 - “We have a big announcement coming up on diesel, I think,” the US president said from the White House.
 - “We stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon,” Trump continued. “The prices will come tumbling, and it’s going to be over soon, one way or the other.”
 - The Trump administration recently pressured European countries to release emergency diesel stocks to help ease soaring diesel prices.
 - Gulf countries Qatar and Kuwait have condemned attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on King Khalid airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh.
 - The attacks by the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), resulted in the death of three Saudi nationals and damage to property.
 - In a statement posted on X, Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said the attacks “represent a grave violation of the Kingdom’s sovereignty and a direct threat to the security of the region and the safety of civilians, civil objects, and air navigation”.
 - Qatar expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and said it supported Saudi Arabia’s “legitimate measures taken to maintain its sovereignty, security, and the safety” and that of all Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.

 - An Israeli drone strike has targeted a car in the Bekaa valley near Lebanon’s border with Syria.
 - The attack happened in Hosh al-Sayed Ali in the Hermel district according to Lebanon’s state media outlet, National News Agency (NNA).
 - Images of the strike circulating on social media appear to show the vehicle was empty.
 - Israel has conducted strikes in Lebanon, despite a US-brokered framework deal signed between Tel Aviv and Beirut in June.
 - According to the deal, Israel troops aimed to withdraw from southern Lebanon and Lebanese military deploy in vacated areas.
 - The deal also tasked Lebanon with disarming the Lebanese armed group Hezbollah.
 - Khaled Batarfi, a Saudi political analyst and author, has questioned the legitimacy of Yemen’s Houthis as Saudi Arabia helps to mount a military campaign against the group.
 - “Houthis are a terrorist group, not a country,” Batarfi told Al Jazeera.
 - The analyst said the Houthis’ argument that their strikes are in retaliation for sanctions and a blockade against the group is misplaced.
 - “Sanctions were placed by the United Nations, not by Saudi Arabia. And any flights need to be coordinated with the United Nations,” Bartarfi said.
 - He also accused the group of receiving orders from Iran to hit civilian targets.
